title: Job Chapter 21 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Job chapter 21 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Job Chapter 21 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Job Chapter 21.

questions.question: In Job 21, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Job answered and said
Their bull gendereth
Even when I remember
Suffer me that I may speak
questions.correctAnswer: Job answered and said
questions.explanation: The first action in Job 21 is Job answering, as stated in Job 21:1.

questions.question: What does Job ask his friends to do with his speech?
options: Mock on
Hear diligently
Be astonished
Lay your hand upon your mouth
questions.correctAnswer: Hear diligently
questions.explanation: Job asks his friends to 'Hear diligently my speech' in Job 21:2.

questions.question: What does Job request to suffer him to do?
options: Speak
Mock on
Be astonished
Fear
questions.correctAnswer: Speak
questions.explanation: In Job 21:3, Job says, 'Suffer me that I may speak'.

questions.question: To whom does Job say his complaint is not directed?
options: God
Man
His friends
The wicked
questions.correctAnswer: Man
questions.explanation: Job states in Job 21:4, 'As for me, is my complaint to man?'.

questions.question: What does Job say happens when he remembers his situation?
options: He is filled with joy
He is afraid
He mocks
He rejoices
questions.correctAnswer: He is afraid
questions.explanation: Job expresses in Job 21:6 that 'Even when I remember I am afraid'.

questions.question: What question does Job pose about the wicked?
options: Why do they suffer?
Wherefore do they live?
When will they die?
How do they prosper?
questions.correctAnswer: Wherefore do they live?
questions.explanation: Job asks in Job 21:7, 'Wherefore do the wicked live?'.

questions.question: What is said about the offspring of the wicked?
options: They are lost
They are established
They are scattered
They are cursed
questions.correctAnswer: They are established
questions.explanation: Job states in Job 21:8 that 'Their seed is established in their sight'.

questions.question: What does Job say about the houses of the wicked?
options: They are filled with fear
They are safe from fear
They are destroyed
They are built on sand
questions.correctAnswer: They are safe from fear
questions.explanation: In Job 21:9, it is mentioned that 'Their houses are safe from fear'.

questions.question: What do the wicked's animals do according to Job?
options: Fail to breed
Gender and calve
Are taken away
Are sickly
questions.correctAnswer: Gender and calve
questions.explanation: Job notes in Job 21:10 that 'Their bull gendereth, and faileth not; their cow calveth'.

questions.question: What do the children of the wicked do?
options: Dance
Cry
Hide
Fight
questions.correctAnswer: Dance
questions.explanation: Job mentions in Job 21:11 that 'Their little ones... dance'.

questions.question: What musical instruments do the wicked take?
options: Drums and flutes
Timbrel and harp
Trumpets and violins
Guitars and pianos
questions.correctAnswer: Timbrel and harp
questions.explanation: In Job 21:12, it states 'They take the timbrel and harp'.

questions.question: Is Job's complaint directed to man?
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Job clearly states in Job 21:4 that his complaint is not to man.

questions.question: Do the children of the wicked rejoice?
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Job states in Job 21:11 that their children dance, indicating they rejoice.

questions.question: Job says that the wicked are punished in this life.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The text does not say that the wicked are punished; rather, it discusses their prosperity.

questions.question: Job expresses joy at remembering his situation.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Job expresses fear when he remembers his situation in Job 21:6.

medium.title: Job Chapter 21 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Job Chapter 21 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Job 21:13, how do the wicked spend their days before going down to the grave?
options: They spend their days in wealth, and in a moment go down to the grave.
They suffer hardship and die slowly.
They live in poverty and die young.
They serve God faithfully until the end.
questions.correctAnswer: They spend their days in wealth, and in a moment go down to the grave.
questions.explanation: Job 21:13 explicitly states, 'They spend their days in wealth, and in a moment go down to the grave.'

questions.question: What does Job 21:19 promise will happen if God 'layeth up' iniquity for someone, as discussed in Job 21:18?
options: He rewardeth him, and he shall know it.
He will immediately forgive him.
He will bless the person abundantly.
He will forget the iniquity completely.
questions.correctAnswer: He rewardeth him, and he shall know it.
questions.explanation: Job 21:19 says, 'God layeth up his iniquity for his children: he rewardeth him, and he shall know it,' indicating consequences follow stored-up iniquity as introduced in Job 21:18.

questions.question: What do the wicked say to God according to Job 21:14?
options: Depart from us; for we desire not the knowledge of thy ways.
Help us in our times of trouble.
We will serve you with all our hearts.
Teach us your righteous paths.
questions.correctAnswer: Depart from us; for we desire not the knowledge of thy ways.
questions.explanation: Job 21:14 records the words of the wicked as, 'Therefore they say unto God, Depart from us; for we desire not the knowledge of thy ways.'

questions.question: How do Job 21:17 and Job 21:18 together describe the fate of the wicked?
options: Their candle is often put out and they are like stubble before the wind.
They live long and prosper in peace.
They are protected by God in times of trouble.
They always repent and turn to righteousness.
questions.correctAnswer: Their candle is often put out and they are like stubble before the wind.
questions.explanation: Job 21:17 says, 'How oft is the candle of the wicked put out!' and Job 21:18 continues, 'They are as stubble before the wind,' together illustrating sudden destruction.

questions.question: What attitude toward God is expressed in Job 21:15, and how does it challenge practical Christian obedience?
options: It questions the benefit of serving God and praying to Him.
It expresses joy in serving God wholeheartedly.
It encourages constant prayer and trust in God.
It praises the Almighty as the source of all blessings.
questions.correctAnswer: It questions the benefit of serving God and praying to Him.
questions.explanation: Job 21:15 asks, 'What is the Almighty, that we should serve him? and what profit should we have, if we pray unto him?' reflecting doubt about the value of obedience and prayer.

questions.question: According to Job 21:16, what is Job's stance toward the counsel of the wicked?
options: The counsel of the wicked is far from me.
I embrace the counsel of the wicked.
I am confused by the counsel of the wicked.
The counsel of the wicked is helpful to me.
questions.correctAnswer: The counsel of the wicked is far from me.
questions.explanation: Job 21:16 states, 'Lo, their good is not in their hand: the counsel of the wicked is far from me,' showing Job's rejection of wicked advice.

questions.question: How does Job 21:20 describe the consequences that the wicked will face?
options: His eyes shall see his destruction, and he shall drink of the wrath of the Almighty.
He shall live in peace and enjoy prosperity.
He shall be forgiven and restored.
He shall be honored by all people.
questions.correctAnswer: His eyes shall see his destruction, and he shall drink of the wrath of the Almighty.
questions.explanation: Job 21:20 clearly states the fate of the wicked as seeing destruction and drinking the wrath of God.

questions.question: What question does Job 21:22 raise about human understanding of God?
options: Shall any teach God knowledge? seeing he judgeth those that are high.
Can man understand the wisdom of God completely?
Is God distant from human affairs?
Does God prefer the humble over the mighty?
questions.correctAnswer: Shall any teach God knowledge? seeing he judgeth those that are high.
questions.explanation: Job 21:22 asks rhetorically if anyone can teach God knowledge, emphasizing His sovereignty in judgment.

questions.question: What contrast does Job 21:23-24 make about the death of some people?
options: One dieth in his full strength, being wholly at ease and quiet; his breasts are full of milk, and his bones are moistened with marrow.
One dies young after a life of suffering and pain.
One dies after a long illness and hardship.
One dies in exile and loneliness.
questions.correctAnswer: One dieth in his full strength, being wholly at ease and quiet; his breasts are full of milk, and his bones are moistened with marrow.
questions.explanation: Job 21:23-24 describes a person dying at peace and in strength, emphasizing the unexpected nature of death.

questions.question: How does Job 21:21 question the value of earthly pleasures for the wicked after death?
options: For what pleasure hath he in his house after him, when the number of his months is cut off in the midst?
He will enjoy everlasting rest in his house.
His wealth will be passed down to his children.
He will be remembered fondly by his family.
questions.correctAnswer: For what pleasure hath he in his house after him, when the number of his months is cut off in the midst?
questions.explanation: Job 21:21 questions the lasting value of earthly possessions when life is cut short.

questions.question: What practical lesson about prayer and service to God can be drawn from the attitude described in Job 21:14-15?
options: Rejecting knowledge of God's ways leads to questioning the benefit of serving Him.
Praying to God always guarantees material wealth.
Serving God is unnecessary because life is unpredictable.
God rewards only those who serve Him for profit.
questions.correctAnswer: Rejecting knowledge of God's ways leads to questioning the benefit of serving Him.
questions.explanation: Job 21:14-15 show that turning away from God's ways results in doubting the value of prayer and service.

questions.question: What does Job 21:17 reveal about God's role in the destruction of the wicked?
options: God distributeth sorrows in his anger.
God always protects the wicked from harm.
God ignores the wicked completely.
God rewards the wicked with long life.
questions.correctAnswer: God distributeth sorrows in his anger.
questions.explanation: Job 21:17 states that God distributes sorrows in His anger, indicating divine judgment on the wicked.

questions.question: How does Job 21:19-20 describe the certainty of consequences for the wicked and their offspring?
options: God layeth up his iniquity for his children; he rewardeth him, and he shall know it. His eyes shall see his destruction, and he shall drink of the wrath of the Almighty.
The wicked are forgiven and their children prosper.
The wicked enjoy peace and their children are blessed.
God forgets the sins of the wicked quickly.
questions.correctAnswer: God layeth up his iniquity for his children; he rewardeth him, and he shall know it. His eyes shall see his destruction, and he shall drink of the wrath of the Almighty.
questions.explanation: Job 21:19-20 clearly depict the stored consequences for sin affecting the wicked and their descendants.

questions.question: True or False: According to Job 21:22, humans can teach God knowledge because He judges only the lowly.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Job 21:22 states, 'Shall any teach God knowledge? seeing he judgeth those that are high,' meaning God judges the mighty and cannot be taught by humans.

questions.question: True or False: Job 21:23-24 describes a person dying in weakness and distress.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Job 21:23-24 describes someone dying 'in his full strength, being wholly at ease and quiet,' not in weakness.

hard.title: Job Chapter 21 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Job Chapter 21.

questions.question: According to Job 21:25, how does another person die in contrast to one who is at ease?
options: In the bitterness of his soul, and never eateth with pleasure
In peace and surrounded by family
In a sudden accident without warning
In the fullness of strength and joy
questions.correctAnswer: In the bitterness of his soul, and never eateth with pleasure
questions.explanation: Job 21:25 states, 'And another dieth in the bitterness of his soul, and never eateth with pleasure,' contrasting with those who die in peace.

questions.question: What happens to both the one who dies in bitterness and the one who dies at ease according to Job 21:26?
options: They shall lie down alike in the dust, and the worms shall cover them
They shall be resurrected immediately
They shall be separated in their graves
They shall ascend to heaven
questions.correctAnswer: They shall lie down alike in the dust, and the worms shall cover them
questions.explanation: Job 21:26 explains that both kinds of people 'shall lie down alike in the dust, and the worms shall cover them,' emphasizing the inevitability of death.

questions.question: What does Job claim to know about his friends' intentions in Job 21:27?
options: I know your thoughts, and the devices which ye wrongfully imagine against me
I do not understand your kindness and generosity
I am unaware of your true feelings
I accept your counsel with gratitude
questions.correctAnswer: I know your thoughts, and the devices which ye wrongfully imagine against me
questions.explanation: Job 21:27 states, 'Behold, I know your thoughts, and the devices which ye wrongfully imagine against me,' showing Job's awareness of their accusations.

questions.question: In Job 21:28, what question do Job's friends ask regarding the wicked?
options: Where is the house of the prince? and where are the dwelling places of the wicked?
Why do the wicked prosper in this world?
When will the wicked be punished?
Who can save the wicked from their sins?
questions.correctAnswer: Where is the house of the prince? and where are the dwelling places of the wicked?
questions.explanation: Job 21:28 records Job's friends asking, 'Where is the house of the prince? and where are the dwelling places of the wicked?' questioning their lasting legacy.

questions.question: According to Job 21:29, who does Job suggest should be asked about the fate of the wicked?
options: Them that go by the way
The priests and scribes
The angels in heaven
The prophets and seers
questions.correctAnswer: Them that go by the way
questions.explanation: Job 21:29 says, 'Have ye not asked them that go by the way? and do ye not know their tokens,' referring to common travelers as witnesses.

questions.question: What is the destiny of the wicked as described in Job 21:30?
options: The wicked is reserved to the day of destruction; they shall be brought forth to the day of wrath
The wicked shall live long and prosper
The wicked will find peace in the afterlife
The wicked shall be forgotten and erased from memory
questions.correctAnswer: The wicked is reserved to the day of destruction; they shall be brought forth to the day of wrath
questions.explanation: Job 21:30 declares the wicked are 'reserved to the day of destruction; they shall be brought forth to the day of wrath,' indicating divine judgment.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'mar' (מָר) in Job 21:25 mean?
options: Bitterness
Joy
Strength
Wisdom
questions.correctAnswer: Bitterness
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'mar' (מָר) in Job 21:25 means 'bitterness,' reflecting the sorrowful state of the soul mentioned there.

questions.question: Which literary device is predominantly used in Job 21:33, 'The clods of the valley shall be sweet unto him, and every man shall draw after him, as there are innumerable before him'?
options: Parallelism
Chiasm
Metaphor
Allegory
questions.correctAnswer: Parallelism
questions.explanation: Job 21:33 employs parallelism, a common Hebrew poetic device, balancing the ideas of death and the multitude that follows.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of the inevitability of death as expressed in Job 21:26?
options: Hebrews 9:27
John 3:16
Romans 8:38
Matthew 5:3
questions.correctAnswer: Hebrews 9:27
questions.explanation: Hebrews 9:27 states, 'it is appointed unto men once to die,' which echoes Job 21:26's theme that all lie down in the dust and are covered by worms.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage connects to the theme of the wicked being reserved for the day of destruction as in Job 21:30?
options: Psalm 37:38
Genesis 1:1
Exodus 20:12
Proverbs 3:5
questions.correctAnswer: Psalm 37:38
questions.explanation: Psalm 37:38 speaks of the wicked being destroyed and their memory perishing, paralleling Job 21:30's depiction of the wicked reserved for destruction.

questions.question: What verse immediately precedes Job 21:25 in the chapter?
questions.explanation: Job 21:24 directly precedes verse 25; it describes one dying with full strength and moisture in the bones before the contrasting statement in 21:25.

questions.question: What is the significance of the phrase 'the clods of the valley shall be sweet unto him' in Job 21:33 in terms of ancient Near Eastern burial customs?
options: It reflects the customary respect and peaceful rest associated with burial grounds
It suggests the valley soil was used for medicinal purposes
It indicates a curse upon the land where the wicked are buried
It symbolizes a ritual feast held at gravesites
questions.correctAnswer: It reflects the customary respect and peaceful rest associated with burial grounds
questions.explanation: Job 21:33's phrase reflects cultural respect for burial sites, indicating peaceful rest, consistent with ancient Near Eastern customs of honoring the dead.

questions.question: How does Job 21:34 use irony as a literary device in addressing his friends' comfort?
options: By stating 'How then comfort ye me in vain, seeing in your answers there remaineth falsehood,' Job ironically highlights their unhelpful and deceitful counsel
By praising their comfort as genuine and helpful
By quoting a proverb that supports his friends' views
By ignoring their comfort entirely
questions.correctAnswer: By stating 'How then comfort ye me in vain, seeing in your answers there remaineth falsehood,' Job ironically highlights their unhelpful and deceitful counsel
questions.explanation: Job 21:34 uses irony to expose the futility and falsehood in his friends' attempts to comfort him.

questions.question: Does Job 21:22 affirm that humans can teach God knowledge?
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Job 21:22 states, 'Shall any teach God knowledge?' implying that no one can instruct God, affirming His supreme wisdom.

questions.question: Is it true that Job 21:23 describes one dying in full strength, being wholly at ease and quiet?
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Job 21:23 explicitly states, 'One dieth in his full strength, being wholly at ease and quiet,' describing peaceful death.

theological.title: Job Chapter 21 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Job Chapter 21 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Job 21:7 teach about the prosperity of the wicked?
options: The wicked live and become old, showing that temporal blessing is not a sign of God's favor
The wicked are immediately punished by God for their sins
The wicked suffer loss and distress as a sign of God's judgment
The wicked prosper only through secret divine blessing
questions.correctAnswer: The wicked live and become old, showing that temporal blessing is not a sign of God's favor
questions.explanation: Job 21:7 states, 'Wherefore do the wicked live, become old, yea, are mighty in power?' showing that wickedness does not preclude earthly prosperity, challenging simplistic retributive justice views.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine judgment is taught in Job 21:17?
options: God distributes sorrows in his anger but does not always punish the wicked immediately
The wicked are always immediately destroyed after sinning
God is indifferent to the fate of the wicked
The wicked prosper without ever facing consequences
questions.correctAnswer: God distributes sorrows in his anger but does not always punish the wicked immediately
questions.explanation: Job 21:17 says, 'How oft is the candle of the wicked put out! and how oft cometh their destruction upon them! God distributeth sorrows in his anger,' indicating that judgment can be delayed and is purposeful.

questions.question: What doctrine of human mortality and equality before death does Job 21:26 teach?
options: All, both the wicked and the righteous, lie down alike in the dust before God
Only the wicked are humbled by death
The righteous live on forever without death
Death is a punishment exclusively for sinners
questions.correctAnswer: All, both the wicked and the righteous, lie down alike in the dust before God
questions.explanation: Job 21:26 states, 'They shall lie down alike in the dust, and the worms shall cover them,' showing universal mortality regardless of moral status.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Job 21:22 specifically demonstrate?
options: Omniscience
Immutability
Justice
Mercy
questions.correctAnswer: Omniscience
questions.explanation: Job 21:22 says, 'Shall any teach God knowledge? seeing he judgeth those that are high,' demonstrating God's all-knowing nature.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is emphasized in Job 21:30 regarding the fate of the wicked?
options: Sovereignty
Omnipotence
Longsuffering
Holiness
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty
questions.explanation: Job 21:30 states, 'That the wicked is reserved to the day of destruction? they shall be brought forth to the day of wrath,' highlighting God's sovereign control over judgment timing.

questions.question: How does Job 21 connect to broader biblical themes of divine justice and human suffering?
options: It challenges simplistic retributive justice, anticipating New Testament teachings on suffering and grace
It affirms that all suffering is direct punishment for sin
It denies any ultimate divine justice
It teaches that prosperity always indicates God's approval
questions.correctAnswer: It challenges simplistic retributive justice, anticipating New Testament teachings on suffering and grace
questions.explanation: Job 21 questions the prosperity of the wicked and shows the complexity of divine justice, a theme developed later in Scripture (e.g., Romans 5:3-5).

questions.question: In what way does Job 21:14-15 anticipate redemptive-historical truths about human rebellion against God?
options: They reject God’s knowledge and question the profit of serving Him, mirroring humanity’s fall into sin and rejection of divine authority
They declare joyful submission to God’s ways
They teach that salvation is earned by works
They deny God's existence
questions.correctAnswer: They reject God’s knowledge and question the profit of serving Him, mirroring humanity’s fall into sin and rejection of divine authority
questions.explanation: Verses 14-15 show the wicked saying, 'Depart from us; for we desire not the knowledge of thy ways' and questioning the Almighty, reflecting humanity's rebellion foundational to biblical sin doctrine.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Job 21:23 and 21:25 teach about the human condition and divine sovereignty over life?
options: God sovereignly determines both peaceful death and bitter death, showing human mortality’s unpredictability
Only the wicked die bitterly while the righteous die peacefully
Human life length is entirely random, without divine control
All humans die peacefully if they are righteous
questions.correctAnswer: God sovereignly determines both peaceful death and bitter death, showing human mortality’s unpredictability
questions.explanation: Verse 23 describes one dying 'in his full strength, being wholly at ease,' while verse 25 shows another dying 'in the bitterness of his soul,' demonstrating God's sovereign control over diverse human experiences.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning divine justice and human accountability is taught by Job 21:19 and 21:20 together?
options: God stores up iniquity for the wicked and they will ultimately experience His wrath
The wicked escape all judgment
God is indifferent to sin
Judgment is immediate and public
questions.correctAnswer: God stores up iniquity for the wicked and they will ultimately experience His wrath
questions.explanation: Job 21:19-20 says, 'God layeth up his iniquity for his children... His eyes shall see his destruction, and he shall drink of the wrath of the Almighty,' teaching ultimate accountability.

questions.question: What combined doctrine about human wisdom and divine omniscience is taught by Job 21:27 and 21:28?
options: God knows the wrongful thoughts and devices of humans, revealing His omniscience over human schemes
Humans can hide their thoughts from God
God is unaware of human intentions
Human wisdom can surpass divine knowledge
questions.correctAnswer: God knows the wrongful thoughts and devices of humans, revealing His omniscience over human schemes
questions.explanation: In verses 27-28, Job states he knows their thoughts, but God judges those devices, showing divine omniscience over human plans.

questions.question: Sceptics claim Job 21:29-34 teaches that the wicked escape judgment. What does this passage actually teach?
options: The wicked are reserved for destruction and will face the day of wrath, but their destruction is sometimes delayed
The wicked always prosper and never face consequences
God arbitrarily punishes only some sinners
The wicked are rewarded after death
questions.correctAnswer: The wicked are reserved for destruction and will face the day of wrath, but their destruction is sometimes delayed
questions.explanation: Verses 29-30 state the wicked are reserved to the day of destruction and brought forth to the day of wrath, affirming eventual divine judgment despite temporal prosperity.

questions.question: What doctrine of human fear and spiritual distress is taught in Job 21:6?
options: Remembering past sufferings causes trembling and fear in the human body and spirit
Humans are immune to fear when recalling pain
Spiritual distress is unrelated to physical fear
Fear is a sign of divine disfavor
questions.correctAnswer: Remembering past sufferings causes trembling and fear in the human body and spirit
questions.explanation: Job 21:6 says, 'Even when I remember I am afraid, and trembling taketh hold on my flesh,' teaching that human memory of suffering evokes deep fear and bodily response.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is especially highlighted in Job 21:32 regarding the fate of all humans?
options: Immutability
Justice
Mercy
Sovereignty
questions.correctAnswer: Immutability
questions.explanation: Job 21:32 states, 'Yet shall he be brought to the grave, and shall remain in the tomb,' highlighting the unchanging reality of death as part of God's created order.

questions.question: How does Job 21:12-13 prepare the reader for the biblical teaching on the fleeting nature of earthly joy?
options: The wicked rejoice in music and wealth, but their enjoyment ends abruptly at death, illustrating life’s transitory nature
The wicked experience eternal joy
Earthly joy is permanent and guaranteed by God
Music and wealth are signs of divine blessing without end
questions.correctAnswer: The wicked rejoice in music and wealth, but their enjoyment ends abruptly at death, illustrating life’s transitory nature
questions.explanation: Verses 12-13 describe the wicked rejoicing and spending their days in wealth but then going down quickly to the grave, underscoring life’s brevity.

questions.question: What combined doctrine about human sin and its consequences is taught by Job 21:14 and 21:34?
options: Rejecting God’s ways leads to false comfort and vain answers, highlighting the futility of ungodly counsel
Rejecting God leads to true comfort and peace
Falsehood and vanity only come from the righteous
God’s ways are irrelevant to human comfort
questions.correctAnswer: Rejecting God’s ways leads to false comfort and vain answers, highlighting the futility of ungodly counsel
questions.explanation: Verse 14 shows the wicked saying they desire not God's knowledge, and verse 34 critiques the falsehood in their answers, teaching that rejection of divine truth results in vain counsel.
